meta.title: Organizar la información con clefts
meta.goal: Puedes dividir la información con it-cleft y what-cleft para enfatizar un elemento y controlar el foco informativo con precisión.

cards.title: El orden indica qué debe notar el oyente
cards.lede: Las clefts dividen una idea en dos partes para enfocar una persona, momento, razón o acción.

columns.label: Neutra
examples: Maya approved the budget on Tuesday.

columns.label: It-cleft
examples: It was Maya who approved the budget.
It was on Tuesday that she approved it.

columns.label: Wh-cleft
examples: What Maya approved was the revised budget.

cards.title: Corrige o contrasta un dato
cards.lede: La posición después de be recibe el contraste más fuerte.

rows.value: It was Jordan who caught the error, not the auditor.
It was the shipping fee that surprised me.
It wasn't until midnight that the server came back online.
It was because the deadline changed that we revised the scope.

cards.title: Presenta una necesidad, acción o resultado
cards.lede: What crea un marco conocido y coloca la información focal después de be.

rows.value: What we need is a decision, not another meeting.
What I did was restart the service.
What I'd rather do is test the smaller release first.
What bothered the client most was the lack of updates.

tip.label: Concordancia
tip.body: La forma de be suele concordar con el complemento focal: What we need is time; What we need are two more engineers.

cards.title: Adelanta un elemento para crear contraste
cards.lede: El fronting es marcado: úsalo cuando el contexto ya establece una comparación o un tema.

columns.label: Orden neutral
examples: I had never seen such a careful analysis.

columns.label: Fronting / inversión
columns.rule: Enfoca el elemento inicial; algunos adverbiales exigen inversión.
examples: The schedule I can handle; the budget is another matter.
Never had I seen such a careful analysis.

cards.title: No dupliques el sujeto ni fuerces el foco
cards.lede: La estructura debe tener una función comunicativa clara, no solo sonar más compleja.

lines.text: It was Maya she approved the budget.
It was Maya who approved the budget.
What I need it is more context.
What I need is more context.
It was coffee that I drank this morning.
lines.note: Gramatical, pero innecesariamente marcada sin contraste.
Natural si nadie está corrigiendo qué bebiste.

cards.title: Responde al supuesto equivocado
cards.lede: Antes de elegir una cleft, identifica exactamente qué dato estás corrigiendo.

rows.value: A: The director rejected it. B: Actually, it was the client who rejected it.
A: We need a new tool. B: What we need is clearer ownership.
It wasn't until the second review that we noticed the inconsistency.
Usa una frase neutral si no existe contraste, corrección ni transición temática.

tip.label: Práctica
tip.body: Toma una frase neutral y crea tres it-clefts que enfoquen persona, tiempo y objeto; explica qué supuesto corrige cada una.

quiz.q: Someone says Alex approved the change, but it was Nina. Which reply fits?
options: What Nina was approve the change.
It was Nina who approved the change.
Nina it was who approved the change.
quiz.explain: La it-cleft coloca a Nina en foco y corrige el supuesto sobre la persona.

quiz.q: Complete: What the team needs ___ two uninterrupted days.
quiz.explain: El complemento conceptual two uninterrupted days se presenta como una sola necesidad; is es natural aquí.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses inversion after a negative fronted adverbial?
options: Never I had seen that pattern.
Never had I seen that pattern.
quiz.explain: Never al inicio exige inversión de auxiliar y sujeto.

quiz.q: ¿Cuándo suele ser mejor una frase neutral?
options: Cuando no hay contraste ni corrección que justificar.
Siempre que el hablante quiera sonar avanzado.
Cuando se enfoca explícitamente un dato equivocado.
quiz.explain: Las clefts son estructuras marcadas; deben responder a una necesidad informativa.
